questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Matrix Given Solutions to a Matrix ODE
questions.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=u(t)+v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}({e}^{7t})^{′} \\ ({e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7{e}^{7t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Constructing General Solutions of First-Order Linear Systems of ODEs
questions.problem:
Let ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfy the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)$ and ${x}_{p}(t)$ satisfy the inhomogeneous system
${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)+f(t).$
Which of the following is **always** a solution of the same inhomogeneous system?

- ${x}_{1}(t)-4\cdot {x}_{2}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- $-7\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- $2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+2\cdot {x}_{p}(t)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${x}_{h}(t)$ satisfies a homogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution to an inhomogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t),$ then ${x}_{h}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$ is also a solution to the same inhomogeneous system.

Additonally, the *linearity principle* for systems of linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) states that if ${x}_{1}(t),$ ${x}_{2}(t),…,{x}_{k}(t)$ are solutions to a homogeneous linear system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ then any linear combination 

$$
{c}_{1}{x}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{x}_{2}(t)+⋯+{c}_{k}{x}_{k}(t)
$$

with ${c}_{1},{c}_{2},…,{c}_{k}\in R$ is also a solution of the same homogeneous system. 

With that in mind, let's examine the given expression.

- Option I is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)=1\cdot {x}_{1}(t)-4\cdot {x}_{2}(t)
$$

is a solution to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ according to the linearity principle. Thus, 

$$
{{{x}_{1}(t)-4\cdot {x}_{2}(t)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{h}(t)}+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

is a solution to our inhomogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).$

- Option II is a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Indeed, notice that the linear combination 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)=-7\cdot {x}_{1}(t)
$$

is a solution to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ according to the linearity principle. Thus, 

$$
{{-7\cdot {x}_{1}(t)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{h}(t)}+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

is a solution to our inhomogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t).$

- Option III might be *not* a solution to the inhomogeneous system. Notice that $2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+2\cdot {x}_{p}(t)$ can't be written as 

$$
{x}_{h}(t)+{x}_{p}(t),
$$

where ${x}_{h}(t)$ is a solution of the homogeneous system, because of the multiplier $2$ next to the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
